**How it works:** The first line is `// \`. C++ treats a backslash at the end of a `//` comment as a line continuation, so g++ also comments out the next line, which holds the Rust `main`. Rust sees that next line as ordinary code. A `/*` at the end of the Rust line starts a block comment in both languages. That hides the C++ code from Rust, and the closing `// */` ends the comment.

**Limits:** Both versions use 128-bit unsigned integers, which is exact up to f(185). Beyond that the Rust version wraps around, and so does the C++ version.
